title: Higher cortical and lower subcortical metabolism in detoxified methamphetamine abusers

claims.statement: In one PET study, 15 people abstinent from methamphetamine had 14% higher whole-brain glucose metabolism than 21 controls (p<0.05, while the study set p<0.01 as its threshold), with relatively lower metabolism in the thalamus (17%) and striatum (6–12%); another research group found no difference in global metabolism. Users and controls also differed in smoking (73% vs 24%) and sex ratio, and cognition was tested in users only.
claims.magnitude: Whole brain 38.4 vs 33.6 µmol/100 g/min (+14%, t=2.2, df=34, p<0.05); relative to whole brain: thalamus −17%, caudate −12%, putamen −6%, parietal +5%. Not replicated for global metabolism by London et al. (2004).
